extracted.intended_audience: applicants and organizational representatives submitting federal grant applications via Grants.gov Workspace
extracted.subtask_short: apply for grants via Grants.gov Workspace
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, attaching, submitting, and troubleshooting federal grant application packages using the Grants.gov Workspace system. Covers account/registration, roles, form/attachment rules, technical/browser/security requirements, and support procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) is a unique number assigned to all entities who register to do business with the federal government. UEI numbers are obtained from www.sam.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The federal government transitioned from DUNS to UEI (SAM) per OMB direction; agencies/systems completed transition no later than April 4, 2022. See the U.S. General Services Administration Unique Entity Identifier Update page for up-to-date information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need a Grants.gov account to apply using Workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: You need one Grants.gov account to apply using Workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you work with multiple organizations, you can create and manage multiple profiles within the same Grants.gov account. See the My Account help article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant registration process
rubrics_metrics.description: How to register as a consultant to support clients in Workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register an account on Grants.gov, then the applicant organization(s) can add you as a participant to their workspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can create a workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with the Workspace Manager role can create a workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Workspace Roles page for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can submit a workspace application (AOR roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only users with the Standard Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) role who are added as a Workspace Participant may submit an application. If your organization uses the Expanded AOR role, then any user with the Expanded AOR role may submit any workspace, even if they are not added as a Workspace Participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information, read the Workspace Roles page and the Manage Organization Profile help article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form locking behavior for simultaneous edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Webforms lock to the user who starts working; unlocked PDF forms edited simultaneously may have last-uploaded version overwrite previous changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Workspace Participant clicks the Webform link, Workspace automatically locks the form to that user; a different participant cannot fill out the webform at the same time. For unlocked PDF forms, changes are captured only when the PDF is uploaded, and the last person to upload will overwrite prior uploads—Workspace will prompt before overwrite. Once a form is locked to a participant, other users' attempts to upload will be blocked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previewing your application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can preview the application via the View Application tab in Workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the View Application Tab and Attachments Tab help articles for details on previewing application forms and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted application packages will be retained for 5 years after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statuses Validated, Received By Agency, or Agency Tracking Number Assigned are available for download during this time. Note: the purge period was increased from 180 days to 5 years on October 20, 2015; applications submitted before April 22, 2015 were deleted under the previous 180-day purge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify contents of submitted application package
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should download a copy of the submitted application to verify contents of the submission zip file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download via the Details tab of the workspace and verify each file in the zip. Applicants can download a zip only when the submitted application is in Validated, Received by Agency, or Agency Tracking Number Assigned status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file size limits (agency-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment file size limits vary by award-making agency; refer to the agency's application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov suggests limiting the file size of the entire grant application package including all attachments to 200MB. Always follow the specific agency instructions for any stricter limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Add Attachments button in PDF forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing a PDF form using Adobe software, use only the Add Attachments buttons in the form to attach a document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use other attachment functions built into Adobe Reader or the menu bar, this will cause errors and the attachments will not actually transmit to the federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of attachments and media compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency has restrictions on allowed attachment types (e.g., .pdf, .xls, .docx) and sizes; media files should be compressed for web usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding video (.mpeg, .mov), image (tif, jpg, png), or audio (.wav, .aif, .au), compress appropriately. Check agency instructions for allowed quality, resolution, and bit rate standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplicate attachment filenames
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one attachment has the same name, the application cannot be processed without manual intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rename attached files so no files share the same name, reattach, and resubmit the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default file name restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency/form does not specify file name restrictions, Grants.gov default rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit file names to 50 or fewer characters and use only the following UTF-8 characters: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen, space, period, parenthesis, curly braces, square brackets, ampersand, tilde, exclamation point, comma, semi colon, apostrophe, at sign, number sign, dollar sign, percent sign, plus sign, and equal sign. Noncompliance may cause rejection or processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy/paste caution from Microsoft Word
rubrics_metrics.description: Copying and pasting from Word may lead to errors in the Adobe Reader form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using copy/paste, first copy the information into a plain text editor (Notepad or TextEdit) to remove proprietary fonts or special characters before pasting into the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form field data limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Form fields have set amounts of data they accept; once the limit is reached you cannot enter more data into that field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits vary between agencies and forms; refer to the agency instructions available with the application package for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: UTF-8 special characters in form fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov accepts UTF-8 characters within form fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific agency instructions for guidance regarding the use of special characters to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional district code format
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format the congressional district code for forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2-character state abbreviation, a hyphen, and then a 3-character district number (e.g., CA-005, VA-008). Use 00-000 for programs or projects outside the US. Use House.gov to find district by zip + 4; USPS ZIP+4 lookup if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Center required supporting details for help requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When contacting the Grants.gov Support Center, provide specific supporting details to help troubleshoot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Funding Opportunity Number (FON) or Package ID, Browser Type and Version, Operating System Type and Version, Form Name and Version, Adobe Reader/Acrobat version, Exact Error Message if applicable, Grants.gov Username, and UEI (SAM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Email already exists in system during registration
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive 'Email Already Exists in System' you cannot register with that email again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a new email address or sign into the account using that existing email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Grants.gov profile
rubrics_metrics.description: A profile corresponds to a single applicant organization, an individual applicant, or a single federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you work for or consult with multiple organizations and have a profile for each, you may log in to one Grants.gov account to access all of your workspaces. See Add Profile to a Grants.gov Account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login troubleshooting — locked out and username retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: If locked out from logging in, consult the Login.gov help center for assistance. You can retrieve a forgotten username via the Retrieve Username page or by logging in and checking My Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If account is linked with Login.gov or another authentication service, update account info directly with that service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password reset process
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to reset a forgotten Grants.gov password using a temporary code sent to email or mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter username, choose email or mobile for temporary code, enter Temporary Code, enter new password and confirm, click Submit. If you do not receive the Temporary Code, use Resend Temporary Code or call Grants.gov Support at 1-800-518-4726 or email support@grants.gov for assistance. Grantors should contact their Agency POCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password expiration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov passwords are valid for 60 days and will not be valid on the 61st day onward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your account is linked to Login.gov or another two-factor provider, you will not need the Grants.gov password to log in. After expiration, users log in with Login.gov if linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account deactivation for inactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov accounts are automatically deactivated after 365 days of inactivity (not logging in for a year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov sends four warning emails, one per week for the four weeks before deactivation. If deactivated you will lose all roles in Grants.gov (roles are not applicable to EBiz POCs and individual applicant profiles but those accounts are also deactivated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps after account deactivation
rubrics_metrics.description: What to do after your Grants.gov account is deactivated for inactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log in using the Login.gov button. EBiz POC: no additional steps after logging in and resetting password. Individual Profiles: no additional steps. Organization Profiles: re-activating automatically emails your organization's EBiz POC to assign roles; you may also contact your EBiz POC directly. Grantors must communicate with someone in their grant-making agency with the Manage Agencies role to reassign roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported web browsers
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov supports the latest versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE), Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, and Apple Safari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browsers change frequently—use the latest version. Legacy versions may be functional but may have issues. Grants.gov no longer supports Internet Explorer 9 or below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required security protocols (TLS/SSL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your web browser must support at least one of TLS versions 1.0, 1.1, or 1.2 to access Grants.gov. SSL 2 and 3 are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are disabled in the Training environment and will be disabled in the Production environment in the future; read Grants.gov Notices for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safari pop-up blocker and viewing attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Safari blocks pop-up windows by default, which can prevent viewing attachments in Workspace online webforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow pop-up windows in Safari to view attachments. Instructions: Safari menu → Preferences → Security tab → uncheck 'Block pop-up windows'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to clear browser cache
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions are provided to clear the browser cache (Temporary Internet Files) which can affect Grants.gov behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links are provided to step-by-step instructions for clearing cache in Internet Explorer, Firefox, Chrome, and Safari.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antivirus best practices when using Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Users are responsible for local virus checks when downloading/uploading to help protect against zero-day attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure antivirus software with latest signature updates is installed and running; perform a local scan prior to uploading files; download Workspace data to a temporary folder and scan before opening; report suspicious files/activity immediately to Grants.gov Support Center at 1-800-518-4726 or support@grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available help resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to find additional registration, search, and application instructions and how to contact support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Grants.gov Online User Guide (Applicants section) for detailed information and contact the Grants.gov Support Center via support@grants.gov or the Support page. Additional FAQs and ticket status are available in the Grants.gov Support Center iPortal.
